statusText:
Nothing has traded. The CME weekend halt still governs the published state: NQ futures have not quoted since Friday 14 August and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, about five and a half hours from this run. Tail is 17%, the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path is the thing Tail measures, and it cannot form while no venue is quoting, so the one-point increase over the previous hour is pure time-to-reopen compression rather than anything observed in price.

Stress eases one more point to 79% and, for the first time this weekend, drops out of the extreme band into high. That is an evidence-based easing, not decay: the Times of Israel liveblog now runs to 18:54 local time, 15:54 UTC, roughly half an hour before this run, and carries no new Strait of Hormuz action, no new Gulf or Saudi oil-infrastructure strike and no new Lebanon escalation. Kushner has met President el-Sissi on ceasefire implementation and is heading into direct talks with Hamas leadership in Egypt alongside Egyptian and Qatari officials, and Araghchi has confirmed on the record that Iran-Oman talks on Hormuz shipping routes remain live. The escalatory items that did land in the last three hours - Ben Gvir's remarks and Iran's $30,000 bounty on US soldiers - are rhetoric without a transmission channel into Nasdaq-100 pricing.

Stress stays high rather than falling further because the backdrop is genuinely unresolved. Hormuz is still closed, the reopening is explicitly conditioned by Tehran on US compliance with the June memorandum, the IEA is forecasting the widest global supply deficit in five years, and Treasury Secretary Bessent has said the unprecedented Iran 'economic isolation' package will be unveiled this coming week. That is an unscheduled, high-impact catalyst sitting inside the trading week with no fixed timestamp, which is exactly the kind of thing that belongs in Stress and not in Tail.

Confidence is 80%, in the high band. Every reference level in this assessment was re-read from a primary quote page this hour, the seven-day calendar was re-verified against the Trading Economics US calendar, and two independent liveblogs were read for the geopolitical track. The ceiling on confidence is structural: there is no live price path to score, and CNBC and Reuters both refused the fetch this hour.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 17% maps to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always.

The roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window and the danger window is anchored to it, 21:55 UTC to 00:30 UTC on 17 August, 23:55 to 02:30 Berlin. That bracket covers the restart itself plus the first two and a half hours of quoting, which is where a two-day information gap - Hormuz still closed, the pending Bessent package, WTI up 1.42% on Friday - has to resolve into a thin opening book. The forecast steps to WATCH at 21:00 UTC and to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for the 22:00 UTC restart hour on gap mechanics alone, then decays back through the Asian session as live structure replaces inference.

Nothing here is a directional call. The index enters the reopen near but not at extremes - NQU26 2.7% below its 52-week high, QQQ 2.3% below its own - and near-extreme only becomes an amplifier once a persistent one-way path with failed pullbacks is actually observed. Nothing of the sort exists on a closed tape.
headline: Five and a half hours to the Globex restart and the CME weekend halt still governs: Stress eases a point to 79% and leaves the extreme band on a second consecutive quiet, de-escalatory hour - Kushner into direct Hamas talks in Egypt, Iran-Oman Hormuz talks confirmed live, no new escalation since 15:54 UTC - Tail ticks to 17%, EA_ON and green, Confidence 80%
body:
Observed reference levels, all from Friday 14 August's close because nothing has traded since, and all re-verified from primary quote pages this hour. NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, having opened at 30,210.75 and held a 254-point range of 30,028.50 to 30,283.00 on 397,964 contracts; Investing.com still marks the contract Closed as of 14/08. The 52-week range is 22,961.50 to 30,975.50, putting the settlement about 2.7% below the high. On the cash side QQQ closed at $731.07, down $1.00 or 0.14%, opening at $733.26 against a $732.07 previous close with a $728.32 to $734.39 range on 23.5m shares, and a 52-week range of $555.60 to $748.65 - about 2.3% below its own high. Both readings describe an index that finished the week consolidating just under record territory, not one that was extending.

Volatility and rates. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60%, in a 14.18 to 14.72 range against a 14.63 previous close, stamped 14 August 15:15 CDT, and sits near the bottom of its 13.38 to 35.30 52-week range. The 10-year yield closed at 4.696%, up 5.5 basis points or 1.19% from 4.641%, stamped 14 August 13:59 CDT, and is within five basis points of its 4.747% 52-week high. That combination is the single genuine conflict in the evidence set: equity volatility is priced for calm while the long end is pressing the top of its range. It is a Stress input, not a Tail input, because conflicting signals raise the difficulty of the environment without establishing a one-way path.

Energy. WTI is $82.40, up $1.15 or 1.42%, and Brent $88.52, up $1.45 or 1.67%, both stamped 14 August. Trading Economics attributes the strength to the continued US naval blockade and to the IEA warning of the widest global supply deficit in five years, partially offset by the IEA cutting its demand outlook on the view that prolonged conflict and elevated prices are eating into consumption. Crucially, Iran and Oman have not reached agreement on reopening Hormuz despite earlier optimism.

Geopolitics, and this is where the hour actually moved. The Times of Israel liveblog runs to 18:54 local, 15:54 UTC, about half an hour before this run. Between 17:35 and 18:54 local the entries are Israel-Honduras defence cooperation, a Jerusalem synagogue vandalism, a New York synagogue arrest and Ben Gvir's remarks on Gaza - domestic and rhetorical, with no market transmission channel. The market-relevant items are constructive: Kushner met el-Sissi on ceasefire implementation at 16:56 local and is heading into a direct meeting with Hamas leadership in Egypt with Egyptian and Qatari officials. Al Jazeera's liveblog carries Araghchi confirming Iran-Oman talks on Hormuz shipping routes continue, with the caveat that reopening depends on the US honouring the June memorandum. Iran's $30,000 bounty on US soldiers, from 15:42 local, is escalatory in tone but has no pricing channel. Net: a second consecutive hour with no new Hormuz, Gulf-infrastructure or Lebanon escalation, and visible progress on the diplomatic track.

The unresolved catalyst. Bessent said on 13 August that the Trump administration will unveil 'measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country' against Iran, explicitly next week, as a one-two punch alongside the continued Hormuz blockade. The blockade has already cost Tehran roughly $4.8bn in oil revenue. This has no timestamp, cannot be put in the event calendar, and is precisely why Stress stays in the high band rather than continuing to decay: a headline of that class landing intraday would reprice energy and risk appetite simultaneously.

Calendar and catalysts. The seven-day US calendar was re-verified against Trading Economics this hour and is unchanged: Empire State and NAHB Monday, Housing Starts, Building Permits and Industrial Production Tuesday, FOMC Minutes at 18:00 UTC Wednesday, Jobless Claims and the Philadelphia Fed at 12:30 UTC Thursday, and the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC Friday. FOMC Minutes is the only genuinely index-level macro item in the window. Two larger catalysts sit just outside the seven days and are therefore correctly absent from the events array: Nvidia's Q2 FY27 report after the close on Wednesday 26 August, and the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August with Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed chair on the 28th. Both matter for the shape of the second half of the month; neither can affect this window.

Why Tail stays at 17%. Tail measures the probability that mean reversion fails long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid strategy through a persistent no-retracement trend. The v1.1.0 threshold for 25%+ requires observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ holding near extremes, or multiple independent current amplifiers. On a closed tape, none of the observational conditions can be met by construction. The one static amplifier present - the index sitting near, though not at, its 52-week high - is a positioning fact, not a path. 17% represents the residual: a two-day unpriced information set resolving into a single opening print, five and a half hours out.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 16:00 UTC Saturday to 15:00 UTC Sunday and sit entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours and the headline outcome was identical each time: EA_ON, green, dominantMode mixed. Tail never left the low band, drifting from 11% up to 16% in small increments driven by nothing more than the shrinking distance to the Globex restart. Stress carried all the movement and traced a genuine arc: 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75 through the Saturday evening and overnight escalation phase, a dip to 70 and 71 in the early European morning, then a step up to 78, 79, 78, 80, 78, 81 and a peak of 82 at 14:00 UTC as the Hormuz and Bessent threads tightened, before easing to 80 at 15:00 UTC on the first clearly de-escalatory hour. Confidence improved monotonically from 62% to 79% as more primary sources were verified and re-verified across the halt. The important observation for interpreting the current state is that the whole 24-hour band contains zero price observations: every score in it is an assessment of a static information set, and the Stress arc is a record of the news flow, not of any tape.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 15:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart and the first seventeen hours of live quoting sit inside the window, along with Monday's Empire State and NAHB releases and the US cash open. Tail stays in the low band for the six remaining halt slots, drifting 17% to 19%, then steps to 20% at 21:00 UTC immediately before the restart and peaks at 25% in the 22:00 UTC reopen hour - the only slot in the forecast reaching BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, and reaching it on gap mechanics rather than on any expectation of trend. From there it decays through 24%, 22%, 21%, 20% and back into the high teens across the Asian and European sessions, then lifts again to 19%, 23% and 22% around the 12:30 UTC data and the 13:30 UTC cash open before settling at 20%. Stress mirrors that shape at a higher level, easing from 79% to 73% through the quiet hours, bumping to 80% at the restart and to 76% at the cash open. Confidence dips to 76% in the thin, illiquid reopen hour and then climbs steadily to 87% as a live price path finally becomes available to score. The two things that would invalidate this shape are the same two that dominate the current assessment: an early or unusually aggressive Bessent announcement on Iran, or a new Hormuz or Gulf infrastructure event during the Asian session. Either would lift Stress well before it lifted Tail, because Tail requires an observed path and an announcement is not one.

The CME weekend halt still sets the published state: NQ futures have not quoted since Friday 14 August and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC, about five and a half hours from this run. Tail ticks one point to 17% purely as time-to-reopen compression - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue quotes, so the entire move is anticipatory, not observed. Stress eases one more point to 79% and drops out of the extreme band into high: the Times of Israel liveblog now runs to 18:54 local (15:54 UTC) with no new Hormuz, Gulf-infrastructure or Lebanon escalation, Kushner has met el-Sissi and is heading into direct talks with Hamas leadership in Egypt, and Araghchi confirms Iran-Oman shipping talks are still live. Confidence 80% on a full re-verification of NQ, VIX, QQQ, 10Y and oil from primary quote pages.

Still halted, roughly four and a half hours to the restart. Expect no change in substance: Tail holds at 17% and Stress eases a point to 78% if the de-escalatory drift in the liveblogs persists through the European evening. The one thing that would break this is a headline on the Bessent 'economic isolation' package landing early rather than during the week, which would push Stress back toward the low 80s without moving Tail, because an announcement is not a price path.

Third halt hour of the forecast. Tail edges to 18% as the reopen moves inside four hours and the unpriced weekend information set - Hormuz still closed, the IEA supply-deficit warning, WTI at $82.40 and Brent at $88.52 from Friday - has to clear through a single opening print. Stress steady at 78%. This is gap risk, not trend risk, and the distinction is why the status stays green.

Roughly three hours out. Tail 18%, Stress 77%. The quiet Sunday-evening tape in the newsflow is the base case; the calendar is empty until Empire State at 12:30 UTC Monday, so the only thing that can reprice the weekend is a geopolitical headline. Confidence slips slightly to 78% because the primary quote pages are now more than 48 hours stale and there is still no live path to score against.

Two hours to the restart. Tail 19%, the top of the low band, and Stress 77%. Positioning matters here: NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, about 2.7% under its 30,975.50 52-week high, and QQQ closed at $731.07 against a $748.65 high, so the index enters the reopen near - but not at - extremes. Near-extreme is an amplifier only once a one-way path actually forms.

Final halt hour, immediately pre-restart. Tail steps to 20% and the action moves to WATCH with a yellow status, entirely on gap mechanics: a two-day information gap resolving into a thin, illiquid opening book. Stress back up to 78%. This is the checkpoint the danger window brackets, and it is the first slot in this forecast where the published action changes at all.
